scene.label: Interactive 3D lesson network showing the fifty Windows PCs on VLAN 80 and SBD-ADMIN-PC01 in front of the core, with the domain controller, SBD-DHCP01, the issuing CA and the event collector they depend on behind it.
scene.completeCaption: Fifty PCs sit in the Workstations OU, hardened by policy, each with its own Windows LAPS password and machine certificate. 802.1X is enforced on the VLAN 80 ports, and every PC reports its security events to the collector.

nodes.name: 50 Windows PCs
nodes.title: 50 Windows PCs · 10.0.80.100–199
nodes.description: SBD-PC01 to SBD-PC50, cloned from one hashed reference image. The three pilots join in lesson 2 and the rest follow in waves in lesson 6, each landing in the Workstations OU with STIG and firewall policy at first boot.

nodes.name: SBD-ADMIN-PC01
nodes.title: SBD-ADMIN-PC01 · 10.0.60.30
nodes.description: The endpoint administration seat on VLAN 60, a virtual machine on SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 built in course 1.8. The workstation firewall policy allows Remote Desktop and remote management only from here, only SBD Tier 2 Admins may read the fleet’s Windows LAPS passwords, and lesson 7 scans the fleet sample from the SCC copy course 1.8 installed there.

nodes.name: SBD-DC01
nodes.title: SBD-DC01 · 10.0.10.10
nodes.description: Holds the Workstations OU, the delegated join account, and the STIG, local Administrators, firewall, DNS registration, LAPS and wired 802.1X policies linked there. It authenticates each join and stores each PC’s managed password and the DNS records SBD-DHCP01 registers; SBD-DC02 holds the same directory and records.

nodes.name: SBD-DHCP01
nodes.title: SBD-DHCP01 · 10.0.20.10
nodes.description: Leases each PC its address from the 10.0.80.100–199 pool through the core’s relay. Lesson 5 adds the Network Policy Server role here for 802.1X port admission only, so the server stays in the member-server tier.

nodes.name: SBD-SUBCA01
nodes.title: SBD-SUBCA01 · 10.0.30.20
nodes.description: The issuing CA. Lesson 4 widens the SBD Computer Authentication template to the SBD Fleet Computers group through the course 1.6 change process; the machine certificates it issues are what 802.1X checks, and its issued log joins the evidence.

nodes.name: SBD-SYSLOG01
nodes.title: SBD-SYSLOG01 · 10.0.20.20
nodes.description: The course 1.10 event collector. It already receives the domain controllers’ events, so the pilot joins arrive on it; lesson 6 enrols the fleet through SBD Event Sources. It forwards what it collects to SBD-SPLUNK01 for analysis.

flows.label: Tier 2 administration · LAPS and SCC scans

chapters.network: The fifty PCs are planned on VLAN 80, and nothing has joined yet. The Workstations OU on the domain controller already carries the STIG, local Administrators, firewall and DNS registration policy links, below course 1.8’s tier logon GPO, and SBD-ADMIN-PC01 on VLAN 60 is the only management source that policy allows.

Three pilots on VLAN 80 take leases from SBD-DHCP01 through the core’s relay, join sbd.test and read their policy, and SBD-DHCP01 registers their DNS records. The domain controller’s join events travel to SBD-SYSLOG01 for analysis.

Each pilot now keeps its own rotating local administrator password in the directory. SBD-ADMIN-PC01 retrieves one under the Tier 2 rules and uses it once on a pilot, and the pilot resets it after use.

The pilots request machine certificates from SBD-SUBCA01 once they are in SBD Fleet Computers, with no one in the loop. Verification fetches the AIA and CDP files from pki.sbd.test over the register’s publication row, F18.
NPS now runs beside DHCP on SBD-DHCP01. The pilots authenticate with EAP-TLS at their VLAN 80 ports in monitor mode, and NPS logs every grant and failure for the existing event subscription.

All fifty PCs now lease, join, enroll, and authenticate, and each forwards its security events to SBD-SYSLOG01 through SBD Event Sources. With enforcement on, an unenrolled device lands in quarantine VLAN 90, which has no routes.

The finished fleet’s steady paths are shown: leases and 802.1X admission at SBD-DHCP01, domain services on the domain controller, certificates from SBD-SUBCA01, and events to SBD-SYSLOG01. SBD-ADMIN-PC01 scans the sample over remote management; the domain controllers, issuing CA and SBD-DHCP01 are rescanned.
